newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee seen quiet in holiday trading.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee seen quiet in holiday trading.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee opened steady at 56.53 to the dollar on Thursday as traders forecast a lethargic market ahead of next week's Christmas holidays.
"I see it as somewhat lethargic," said a Standard Chartered dealer.
At 0400 GMT the rupee was unchanged at 56.53, It closed at 56.52 on Wednesday.
The Central Bank brought down the dollar by 25 local cents, fixing buying and selling rates at 56.0810 and 57.2140, dealers said.
Overnight call money was at 19 percent, boosted by seasonal pressures, dealers said.
An American Express Bank dealer saw the rupee being confined to a tight range between 56.50 and 56.60 in quiet pre-holiday trading.
The Standard Chartered dealer said the currency's recent firming trend could continue if call rates remained high.
